### **Job Description and Duties**

**ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (LIMITED-TERM) – ANGELES DISTRICT/ NATURAL RESOURCES/ MALIBU CREEK STATE PARK**

  

The Angeles District has an opening for an Environmental Scientist (LT). Under the direction of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), serves as the coordinator for the Angeles District Natural Resources Volunteer Program. The incumbent coordinates, organizes, and oversees volunteer projects focused on habitat restoration, invasive plant removal, and community stewardship. This position provides guidance to ensure ecological goals and safety standards are met, while also building partnerships with community groups, schools, and nonprofits. The position is responsible for volunteer program reporting and contributes to the success of SMMC-funded wildfire recovery initiatives.
  
  
This position is a 12-month Limited-Term position that may be extended and/or become permanent.

The incumbent exercises a high degree of initiative, judgment, and analytical skill in coordinating sensitive and high-priority assignments that require collaboration with internal divisions, the Natural Resources Agency, control agencies, and other stakeholders.
  
  
This position is designated as not telework eligible.

  

Training and Development Assignments may be considered.

  

This position requires a valid Class C driver’s license. You must answer the questions addressing your driver’s license on your application. Ensure you provide your driver’s license number, class, expiration date, and any endorsements and/or restrictions on your application.

The selected candidate is required to submit to a background investigation process utilizing Live Scan fingerprinting prior to appointment.

**State housing is not available.** For further information contact Jacoub Mahshi at (424) 508-0465 or Jacoub.Mahshi@parks.ca.gov.

**This recruitment may be used to fill identical vacancies which may occur within 180 days of the Final Filing Date of this job posting.**

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

Effective July 1, 2025, the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025). PLP 2025 directs that each employee receives a temporary reduction in pay in exchange for PLP 2025 leave credits. The percentage of the temporary salary reduction and the number of PLP 2025 leave credits are determined by the position’s assigned bargaining unit. **The salary range(s) included in this job advertisement do not reflect the temporary salary reduction.** For additional information regarding PLP 2025, please click here.  
  
  
  
  
Work environment is an office/outdoor setting, using computers, telephone and other business equipment. Typical work activities involve frequent and prolonged periods of sitting. Typical work involves extended telephone conversations and keyboard operation. Must meet many deadlines within short time frames. Hand dexterity to use telephone, keyboard and calculators are common requirements. Move about, stand, reach, stoop or bend. Use fine motor skills for computer or office machine use. Lift minimum weight of 25 pounds. Use of hand cart to move supplies over 10 pounds of weight. Requires reaching, twisting, turning, kneeling, bending, stooping, squatting, crouching, grasping and making repetitive hand movements in the performance of daily duties. May involve some exposure to aggressive visitors. Will work outdoors in unpredictable weather ranging from extreme heat to extreme cold. May be required to perform arduous field work in rugged, steep terrain. May encounter wild animals. Must be willing to work weekends, nights, and holidays as necessary. Travel maybe required to meetings, conferences, trainings, and on site project locations and may need to use personal vehicle if State Vehicles are not available.

### **Department Information**

The mission of California State Parks is to provide for the health, inspiration, and education of the people of California by helping to preserve the state's extraordinary biological diversity, protecting its most valued natural and cultural resources, and creating opportunities for high-quality outdoor recreation.

All employees are responsible for contributing to an inclusive, safe, and secure work environment that values diverse cultures, perspectives, and experiences, and is free from discrimination.
